meta.title: What UnLitigate Does — UnLitigate
meta.description: Three parts, one aim: make mediation something people think of first. Awareness is live. A supervised student-mediator pilot is starting in Bhubaneswar and Pune.

hero.heading: Three parts, one aim
hero.body: Make mediation something people think of first. Here is what is live and what is coming — only in our pilot cities for now.

items.heading: Awareness and enquiries
items.body: Reels, posts, this site. We explain mediation in plain language and take enquiries from people who want to understand their options.
items.detail: No courtroom language. Just a clear first explanation.

items.heading: Supervised student mediators
items.body: Training and supervision for students who will facilitate suitable disputes in Bhubaneswar and Pune.
items.detail: Students guide the talk. Accredited oversight stays in the room.

items.heading: Referral partnerships
items.body: Working toward links with university mediation centres, so people can be referred to a trusted room.
items.detail: We work with local centres and universities, starting in our pilot cities.

flow.heading: How a case can move
flow.subheading: An educational path — not a promise that every enquiry becomes a mediation.

items.heading: Spot
items.body: Awareness reaches someone who is stuck, worried, or about to file.

items.heading: Refer
items.body: Partners and centres help them find a suitable next step.

items.heading: Mediate
items.body: In the pilot cities, supervised students guide a conversation.

items.heading: Record
items.body: If both sides agree, the terms are written down and signed.

map.heading: Where we are
map.body: Two pilot cities. The soft marks stand for people who may be about to give up on a dispute: not real cases, and not a count.
map.caption: Illustrative. Not data about real people or places. Pilot in Bhubaneswar and Pune only.
map.hint: Tap a pin, or a city card, to switch.

safeguards.heading: Safeguards
safeguards.subheading: For centres, universities and families — solid enough to scan, calm enough not to feel like a warning.

cards.heading: Supervised
cards.summary: Student mediators work under accredited oversight.
cards.detail: A registered mediator or legal-aid clinic stays responsible. The named supervisor will be listed once confirmed.

cards.heading: Confidential and consent-based
cards.summary: No one is forced into the room.
cards.detail: What is said is treated carefully, with the usual limits of the law. Consent can be withdrawn.

cards.heading: Suitable disputes only
cards.summary: We only take matters where talking can still help.
cards.detail: Violence, fraud, or criminal matters need a different door. We say so plainly.

cards.heading: Agreements in writing
cards.summary: Settlements are written down and signed.
cards.detail: If people agree, the terms are recorded clearly so both sides know what they chose.

leave.heading: We don't take
items: Cases involving abuse or threats, where the two sides cannot talk safely or equally
Disputes where one side does not want to take part
Anything that needs a court's ruling, not an agreement between the two sides
Legal advice, representation or guaranteed outcomes
leave.note: If your matter isn't suitable, we'll say so honestly.

whyNow.heading: Why now
whyNow.body: India's Mediation Act 2023 put mediation on a clearer legal footing. The Mediation Council of India was set up in August 2026. We want to work alongside that shift — helping ordinary people hear about the option, in language that does not feel like a courtroom.

cta.heading: Ready to explore your options?
cta.body: Tell us what's happening. We will share general information about mediation — not a case assessment.
